parameters.jsCode:
// The items a controller's record must contain under GDPR Article 30(1), plus the fields this form adds.
// required = must be filled for COMPLETE; min_chars = shortest acceptable answer. Edit in ropa_checklist after the first run.
const rows = [
  ['activity_name', 'Name of the processing activity', 'Art. 30(1) (record identification)', true, 3, 'A short, unique name, e.g. "Payroll" or "Newsletter".'],
  ['owner_team', 'Owner (controller contact / responsible team)', 'Art. 30(1)(a)', true, 2, 'Who answers for this activity inside the organisation.'],
  ['controller_role', 'Role: controller, processor or joint controller', 'Art. 30(1), Art. 30(2)', true, 3, 'Processors keep a different record (Art. 30(2)); this form registers controller activities.'],
  ['purposes', 'Purposes of the processing', 'Art. 30(1)(b)', true, 20, 'Say what the data is used for, specifically. "Various business purposes" is not a purpose.'],
  ['legal_basis', 'Legal basis', 'Art. 6(1); Art. 9(2) for special categories', true, 3, 'One of the Art. 6(1) grounds. Special categories also need an Art. 9(2) condition, stated in purposes or security_measures.'],
  ['data_subjects', 'Categories of data subjects', 'Art. 30(1)(c)', true, 5, 'Customers, employees, applicants, visitors, patients...'],
  ['data_categories', 'Categories of personal data', 'Art. 30(1)(c)', true, 5, 'Contact data, contract data, payment data, health data...'],
  ['recipients', 'Categories of recipients', 'Art. 30(1)(d)', true, 5, 'Internal teams, processors, authorities, group companies. "None" is an acceptable answer if true.'],
  ['transfers_outside_eea', 'Transfers to third countries', 'Art. 30(1)(e); Art. 44-49', true, 2, 'Yes, No or Not sure. Yes needs a safeguard.'],
  ['transfer_safeguard', 'Transfer safeguard', 'Art. 30(1)(e); Art. 46', false, 2, 'Adequacy decision, standard contractual clauses, binding corporate rules, or not applicable.'],
  ['retention_period', 'Envisaged retention period', 'Art. 30(1)(f)', true, 3, 'A period or a rule tied to an event, e.g. "6 years after contract end". "As long as needed" is not a period.'],
  ['security_measures', 'Technical and organisational security measures', 'Art. 30(1)(g); Art. 32', true, 20, 'Access control, encryption, backups, training, vendor DPAs.']
];
return rows.map(r => ({ json: { field_key: r[0], label: r[1], article: r[2], required: r[3], min_chars: r[4], guidance: r[5] } }));

messageValues.message: You review records of processing activities for a privacy team. Raise a point only when you can quote, word for word, the answer in the record that is wrong or too vague; never invent facts, never repeat what the rules already found, and never say a record is fine. Reply with JSON matching the requested schema and nothing else.

## Register processing activities for GDPR Article 30

### How it works
A form registers one processing activity with the items Article 30(1) asks for, from purposes and legal basis to recipients, transfers, retention and security measures. The checklist lives in an editable data table and a Set node holds the vague-phrase lists. A Code node checks the record deterministically: required items present, transfers outside the EEA with a named safeguard, special categories with an Article 9 condition, a legal basis chosen, a retention that is a period, a specific purpose. Hard misses give INCOMPLETE, soft points give REVIEW, a clean record gives COMPLETE, and an empty checklist table gives INCOMPLETE rather than a quiet pass. A Groq reviewer may add a point only with a verbatim quote from the record, so it can raise COMPLETE to REVIEW and never clear a rule. The record goes to ropa_register with a completeness score and the report, each point to ropa_findings. Anything not COMPLETE goes to Discord, and the form shows a page either way. Every Monday a digest counts the register and names the incomplete activities.

### Setup
1. Add a Groq credential to the Groq node and a Discord webhook credential to both Discord nodes.
2. Run Set Up Tables once: it creates the three tables and loads the checklist. Every other node finds its table by name.
3. Register an activity; try one with transfers outside the EEA and no safeguard.
4. Tune Set Register Policy and the checklist rows. Activate the workflow for the Monday digest.

### Customization tips
Add a checklist row and a form field with the same key for anything else your DPO wants. The rules are string checks; the reviewer is a model that can miss things. A register aid, not legal advice.

## 1. Create the tables and load the checklist (run once)
Three tables with typed columns, or reused if the names exist. The twelve Article 30 checklist rows are upserted by key, so running this twice changes nothing. [Data table node docs](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.datatable/)

## 2. Register and check
The [form](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.formtrigger/) collects the record. Set Register Policy holds the vague-phrase lists. Required items, transfer safeguards, the Article 9 condition, the legal basis and the retention wording are checked by rules first.

## 3. Review and decide
The [LLM Chain](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/cluster-nodes/root-nodes/n8n-nodes-langchain.chainllm/) reviewer may add a point only with a verbatim quote that is checked against the record. It can raise COMPLETE to REVIEW, never clear a rule or fill a gap.

## 4. Record
One row per activity in ropa_register with completeness, status and the report; one row per point in ropa_findings with its source and detail, or a none row so every registration leaves a trace.

## 5. Escalate and answer
INCOMPLETE and REVIEW are posted through the [Discord](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/app-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.discord/) webhook, then the form shows the page with the points; COMPLETE shows its own page. Swap Discord for Slack or Gmail.

## 6. Weekly digest
The [Schedule Trigger](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.scheduletrigger/) fires on Mondays once the workflow is active; run it by hand to test. The whole register is counted by status, incomplete activities are named, and a quiet week is said to be quiet.
